tech_stack: C# / ASP.NET Core, SQL Server (Dapper + raw T-SQL), Apache Kafka (Avro), Redis, Azure Blob Storage

owns: Content lifecycle (create, checkout, rename, delete, expire, activate)
depends_on: UMS (User Management Service) — permission and actor resolution
COS (Custom Object Service) — custom object schema
http_deps: UMSServiceProvider — resolves user permissions and actor identity
ProfileServiceProvider — reads and updates content profile assignments
COSClientProvider — fetches custom property schema from Custom Object Service
SeismicKeyClientProvider — manages storage keys for binary assets
TenantInfoProvider — resolves per-tenant configuration and routing
TenantBlobProvider — reads and writes binary assets to Azure Blob Storage
background_services: ExpirationBackgroundService — polls database per region to trigger content expiration jobs
ScheduleActivateBackgroundService — polls for due scheduled activations and executes them
ScheduleAddToProfileBackgroundService — queues content for profile assignment after activation
CustomPropertyBackgroundService — processes custom property schema sync events
SystemStateBackgroundService — maintains content system state derived from events
ContentEventConsumer — consumes content events from CCP meta topic
CustomPropertyEventListener — consumes custom-property schema change events from CMS
VirusScanEventListener — consumes blob virus scan results and updates content state
AugmentationEventListener — consumes static augmentation events from Content Foundation
ExpirationNotificationSettingListener — consumes expiration notification setting changes

domains.name: File & Library Content
domains.responsibility: Manages the full lifecycle of library content files including creation, checkout, rename, move, copy, and soft-delete with ownership enforced per tenant.
domains.health_reason: ItemModel is a 90+ property data bag with public setters and zero behavior; all checkout guards, delete guards, and rename uniqueness rules are implemented as static methods in FileWriter.cs and FileCheckpoint.cs rather than on the aggregate.

invariants: A File cannot be checked out if it is already checked out by another user
A File cannot be deleted while checked out
A File cannot be renamed to a name that already exists in the same folder
A File cannot be activated if it is already in Published status
A File cannot be checked out if it is a folder type

domains.name: Folder
domains.responsibility: Manages folder hierarchy within the library including creation, rename, move, permission assignment, and deletion with structural integrity rules.
domains.health_reason: FolderWriter and FolderCheckpoint are static classes that enforce all folder invariants externally; FolderEntity has no command methods and structural rules such as move-into-descendant prevention live outside the aggregate.

invariants: A folder cannot be renamed to a name that already exists in the same parent
A folder cannot be moved into one of its own descendants
A folder with unique permissions cannot be deleted without explicit permission removal

domains.name: Content Activation & Versioning
domains.responsibility: Controls version lifecycle transitions — publishing, deactivating, and scheduling future activations — with variant and primary-version constraints enforced per content item.
domains.health_reason: ActivationWriter.ActivateContents contains all activation invariant checks (IsPrimary, VersionActivationStage, GroupBy variant uniqueness) inline rather than delegating to ContentVersionEntity aggregate methods.

invariants: A version cannot be activated if it is already in Published status
Cannot activate multiple versions of the same content variant simultaneously
Cannot activate secondary versions when the content has no activated primary version
A scheduled activation cannot be created if one already exists for this version

domains.name: Content Expiration
domains.responsibility: Tracks expiration dates on content items, triggers expiry transitions on schedule, and dispatches pre-expiry notifications to owners based on tenant notification thresholds.
domains.health_reason: ExpirationWriter exists as a class but ContentExpireProcessor and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor determine notification timing and expiry thresholds via inline SQL queries rather than delegating to ContentExpirationEntity.

invariants: Expiration date must be in the future when set
Notification must be sent before expiration date according to tenant notification settings
Content cannot be un-expired once it transitions to expired status

domains.name: Custom Properties
domains.responsibility: Maintains custom property values on content objects, synchronises schema definitions from the Custom Object Service, and removes values when schemas are deleted.
domains.health_reason: CustomPropertyEventListener and COSClientProvider handle schema sync correctly via a background service, but property value validation against schema type is not enforced by an aggregate method — it is checked imperatively in the application layer.

invariants: Property value must conform to the property schema type
Property schema must exist in COS before a value can be set
A deleted property schema must remove all associated values

domains.name: Content Ingestion & Virus Scan
domains.responsibility: Processes uploaded content payloads from VFS and virus scan result events, updating content state and triggering downstream search indexing upon safe-scan confirmation.
domains.health_reason: VirusScanEventListener and ContentEventConsumer apply state changes directly to ItemModel fields without going through aggregate command methods; fire-and-forget Task.Factory.StartNew discards exceptions silently.

invariants: A file cannot transition to active state without a clean virus scan result
A file that fails virus scan must be quarantined and cannot be activated

domains.name: Search & Data Collection Publishing
domains.responsibility: Publishes content change events to search ingestion and data collection Kafka topics so downstream indexers and analytics pipelines remain current.
domains.health_reason: SearchProducer and DataCollectionObserver are called imperatively from within writer classes rather than being dispatched from domain events raised by aggregates, making side-effect completeness depend on each writer author remembering to call both observers.

invariants: A content event must not be published more than once for the same state transition
Library reference events must include all current active versions at point of publish

steps.label: FileCheckpoint.Check — file exists, not folder, not already checked out
FileWriter.CheckoutFileInternal — mutates checkout status outside aggregate
ActivationCheckpoint — version exists, tenant has permission
ActivationWriter.ActivateContents — checks IsPrimary, VersionActivationStage, variant uniqueness inline
ExpirationJobExecutor.Run — iterates tenants, acquires heartbeat lock
ContentExpireNotifyProcessor — inline threshold check, sends notification
ContentExpireProcessor — sets status to expired via direct field mutation
ExpirationNotificationSettingListener — consumes Kafka topic for settings changes
FileCheckpoint.Check — file exists, not checked out
FileWriter.DeleteFile — business rules checked inline in static method
ActivationCheckpoint — no existing schedule, version in valid state
ActivationWriter — creates schedule record inline without aggregate command

gap_analysis.title: Anemic domain model — ItemModel has zero behavior
gap_analysis.detail: ItemModel is a 90+ property data bag with public setters and no methods. All business rules that should live on the aggregate (checkout guard, delete guard, rename uniqueness, folder-type guard) are implemented as static methods in FileWriter.cs and FileCheckpoint.cs. State mutations such as setting checkout status or soft-deleting are performed directly on the DTO by the writer layer with no invariant protection.

gap_analysis.title: Business logic in application layer — ActivationWriter enforces domain invariants
gap_analysis.detail: ActivationWriter.ActivateContents contains multi-line domain rules: it checks item.VersionActivationStage == ContentVersionStatus.Published to throw ActivateActivatedVersionException, verifies variant uniqueness via LINQ GroupBy, and enforces the primary-version-must-exist rule. These are domain invariants that must be enforced inside ContentVersionEntity aggregate methods.

gap_analysis.title: Static writer classes bypass DI — untestable and uninjectable
gap_analysis.detail: FileWriter, ActivationWriter, RenameItemCommon, FolderWriter and 15+ other writer classes are static. Controllers call them directly (FileWriter.AddFile(), FileWriter.DeleteFile()). Context and orchestrators are created via OrchestratorFactory and new ScopedExpressContext() inside the static methods. This makes business logic untestable in isolation and impossible to mock, and means DI-registered services cannot be substituted.

gap_analysis.title: Domain repositories contain raw SQL — infrastructure leaks into domain layer
gap_analysis.detail: FileRepository, ItemRepository, FolderRepository, and 27 other repositories extend SQLDataRepository and embed raw T-SQL strings with SqlParameter arrays. The repositories are located in the domain project (LibraryService.Domain) but are tightly coupled to SQL Server. There is no query abstraction; changing persistence requires touching domain-layer files.

gap_analysis.title: Checkpoint classes externally enforce invariants that belong on aggregates
gap_analysis.detail: 30+ Checkpoint.cs classes in Express.Orchestrator/Checkpoint/ validate preconditions and throw exceptions before reaching any domain object. FileCheckpoint throws FileNotFoundException, FolderCheckpoint throws NoPermissionException. These are domain invariants; they should be enforced by aggregate methods, not by separate static validation classes upstream.

gap_analysis.title: ContentEventConsumer fire-and-forget swallows exceptions and advances offsets incorrectly
gap_analysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer.ConsumeEvent spawns a LongRunning Task via Task.Factory.StartNew with the handle discarded. Exceptions inside RunConsumeAsync are caught only at the inner retry loop; an uncaught exception silently kills the consumer. Kafka offset is committed unconditionally outside the tenant-match branch, meaning events for other tenants are silently dropped but their offsets advance.

gap_analysis.title: No DomainException base class — 280+ raw exception types with no unified HTTP mapping
gap_analysis.detail: All domain exceptions (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, ActivateActivatedVersionException, etc.) extend System.Exception or application-specific bases with no shared DomainException<DomainExceptionType> contract. HTTP status code mapping is scattered across exception handlers. Adding a new exception requires updating multiple middleware layers. There is no DomainExceptionType enum to centralise code-to-HTTP mapping.

gap_analysis.title: OrchestratorFactory static service locator bypasses DI for 40+ orchestrators
gap_analysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.Create*Orchestrator() methods construct orchestrators by resolving services via ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService(). Orchestrators depend on ambient static state, cannot be substituted in tests, and their dependency graph is invisible to the DI container. 40+ orchestrator interfaces are registered in DI but never actually injected — they are retrieved via the factory.

gap_analysis.title: No value objects — status, tenant identity, and compound keys as raw primitives
gap_analysis.detail: Content status is a raw string (item.Status = 'published'), tenant identity is a raw string (teamSiteId), and compound version identity (contentId + versionId + variantId) is passed as separate string parameters everywhere. There are no immutable value objects with validation rules or equality semantics. This allows invalid states (e.g. empty status string, mismatched tenant) to propagate silently through the domain.

gap_analysis.title: ScopedExpressContext created with new inside writers — ambient tenant context not injected
gap_analysis.detail: Every static writer method creates context via new ScopedExpressContext() or new WorkerExpressContext(tenantInfo, userId). This pulls current tenant/user from ambient thread state rather than from a well-defined IExpressContext injected through the request pipeline. Multi-tenancy correctness depends on thread-local state being set correctly upstream, which is fragile and invisible in tests.

gap_analysis.title: Domain events not raised by aggregates — side effects triggered imperatively in writers
gap_analysis.detail: After state changes (file deleted, content activated, content expired) the writers imperatively call observer/producer classes (LibraryContentReferencesObserver.Notify(), SearchProducer.Publish(), DataCollectionObserver.Notify()). There is no domain event raised from an aggregate method that the application service then dispatches. Side effect ordering and completeness depend on each writer remembering to call the right observers.

gap_analysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor contains domain expiry rules that belong on ContentExpirationEntity
gap_analysis.detail: ContentExpireProcessor and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor determine expiry thresholds and notification timing using SQL queries and inline logic rather than through a domain object method. The rule 'notify N days before expiration' is a domain invariant that should live on ContentExpirationEntity, not in a background job executor.

gap_analysis.title: Kafka consumer group ID uses non-production naming convention
gap_analysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer creates a consumer group with GroupId = cms-test-consumer-{topic}. The 'test' infix in a production consumer group ID risks conflicting with actual test consumers and makes observability tooling harder to distinguish environments.

gap_analysis.title: ExpirationBackgroundService uses Thread.Sleep instead of async delay
gap_analysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService calls Thread.Sleep(sleepMillis) inside an async ExecuteAsync method, blocking the thread pool thread for the sleep duration. Should use await Task.Delay() to release the thread during idle periods.

gap_analysis.title: Orchestrator layer duplicates permission checking already done in controllers
gap_analysis.detail: Multiple orchestrators re-validate permissions (tenant access, user role) that are already enforced by the [Authorize] attribute and policy middleware on the controller. This creates divergence risk: a permission change must be applied in two places.
